Q: The reason for the appearance of dark edges that are at sharp angles A:

In your Texture::load code you set the wrap mode to repeat, but for a texture atlas I suggest tex coords should clamp. In the current code any u,v coords just below 0.0 or just above 1.0 which are meant to refer to a texture tile on the edge will instead wrap around to the other side of the texture atlas.

You commented out the code in Map::addFace which adjusts the calculated tex coords by a small eps value. With LINEAR texture filtering I suggest restoring that code, otherwise texture pixels at the edge of a tile will be blended with pixels from the adjacent tile for u,v at the edge.

If anisotropy is currently true, have you tried setting to false?

Q: QT QML How to chain QAbstractListModel and QSortFilterProxyModel A:

By couple of hundred, you mean less than a thousand? Then, a single json payload and doing things in-memory is filtering/sorting should really be fast. The lag you talking about is odd for this number of records. As I said, I've done up to 50,000 with list<var> with no problem.

If you're doing repeated assignments to your model, then, that could be problematic, that could mean you're destroying and recreating 100s of records every refresh. Whereas, if you're able to detect differences and top up the model with incremental updates, then this will result in incremental updates in your UI.

This is what I was alluding to early if the REST endpoint offered you an API that gave you differences per second instead of a data dump, then, the payload would be optimized and so would your code.

Q: Sharing token between apps on Android/IOS A:

Thank you for the suggestion! However, a Custom URL Scheme doesn't fit this specific use case because it requires a 'Push' action from App 1 to App 2.

My requirement is for Silent Discovery (Pull): When a user installs and opens App 2 for the first time, it must autonomously check if App 1 is already logged in.

With a URL Scheme, the user would have to manually open the legacy app and click a 'Migrate' button to trigger the redirection. I need App 2 to 'bootstrap' itself by looking into the shared storage during its first-run initialization, without requiring any interaction with the legacy app.

  1. Bootstrap Check: App 2 only performs this 'discovery' check during the initial launch or if no active session is found. Once the user is logged into App 2, there’s no need to check again.

  2. Fallback: If App 1 is not installed, or if no tokens are found in the shared storage, App 2 simply proceeds to its own standard login screen.

  3. Logout Logic: If the user explicitly logs out of App 2, the app returns to the login state (and could potentially re-check for an App 1 session if needed).

I can't found much information about a feature like that, is like no one use it. haha
